title: Doenjang-Glazed Grilled Black Cod
shortDescription: Rich black cod portions are grilled in a basket with a savory-sweet doenjang glaze divided before raw-fish contact.
culturalContext: Black cod, also sold as sablefish, is not true cod. This doenjang-glazed grilled version is a contemporary Korean-inspired adaptation requiring market-name and language review.
author: {{LEGAL_NAME}}
equipment: Two small bowls for raw-contact and reserved glaze
Outdoor grill or manufacturer-approved indoor electric grill
Fish basket or perforated grill pan

ingredients.preparation: cut into four even portions; pin bones removed

instructions.heading: Inspect and thaw safely
instructions.action: Inspect fish and packaging; thaw overnight in a covered container in the refrigerator if frozen.
instructions.visualOrTactileCue: Fish smells mild, flesh is firm, and packaging is intact.
instructions.safetyNote: Reject sour, rancid, fishy, or ammonia odors and temperature-abused product.

instructions.heading: Dry and portion
instructions.action: Check for pin bones, portion on a dedicated board, and pat every surface dry.
instructions.visualOrTactileCue: Portions are even, dry, and free of detected pin bones.
instructions.safetyNote: Keep raw fish and juices away from ready-to-eat food; wash hands and sanitize tools afterward.

instructions.heading: Mix and divide the glaze
instructions.action: Whisk doenjang, rice syrup, water, vinegar, garlic, and sesame oil smooth, then divide before handling fish.
instructions.visualOrTactileCue: The glaze is smooth and divided before raw contact.
instructions.safetyNote: Keep the reserved finishing portion in a clean labeled bowl away from raw fish.

instructions.heading: Preheat the grill
instructions.action: Preheat a clean fish basket or perforated pan over medium heat and oil it lightly.
instructions.visualOrTactileCue: The surface is hot, clean, and lightly oiled.
instructions.safetyNote: Never use a fuel-burning grill indoors; follow electric-grill ventilation instructions.

instructions.heading: Grill and verify
instructions.action: Place fish skin-side down, brush lightly with raw-contact glaze, cover and grill without turning until opaque and 145°F / 63°C; shield from flare-ups caused by rich fish oils.
instructions.visualOrTactileCue: Fish is opaque, separates easily, and reaches 145°F / 63°C in the thickest portion.
instructions.safetyNote: Use clean tools after the final turn and verify temperature with a clean calibrated thermometer.

instructions.heading: Finish and serve
instructions.action: Transfer to a clean platter, brush only with the clean reserved glaze, rest 2 minutes, and serve promptly.
instructions.visualOrTactileCue: The fish is glazed on a clean platter and served hot.
instructions.safetyNote: Refrigerate within 2 hours and warn diners that pin bones may remain.

grillSetup: Use an outdoor grill or approved indoor electric grill with a clean, lightly oiled fish basket or perforated pan over medium heat and an open cooler area.
targetInternalTemperature: 145°F / 63°C in the thickest portion; visual cues supplement but do not replace thermometer verification.
visualDonenessCues: Fish separates easily with gentle pressure
foodSafetyNotes: Buy fish cold and keep at or below 40°F / 4°C.
Thaw in the refrigerator or by an FDA-approved rapid method and cook immediately.
Prevent raw-fish cross-contact and reserve finishing glaze before raw contact.
Cook to 145°F / 63°C and warn that pin bones may remain.

allergens.crossContactWarning: Contains fish, soy, wheat/gluten, and sesame; doenjang formulas vary, so verify the label.

substitutions: Use a verified gluten-free doenjang only after test-cook adjustment for salt and viscosity.
ingredientSourcing: Confirm the product is black cod/sablefish, kept cold, with firm flesh and mild odor.
makeAhead: Mix glaze up to 2 days ahead; divide it before raw contact. Portion and glaze fish only within the stated refrigerated window.
storage: Refrigerate cooked fish in a shallow covered container within 2 hours and use within 3 days pending food-safety approval.
reheating: Reheat only the needed portion to 165°F / 74°C until steaming.
leftovers: Use properly refrigerated leftovers within the approved window; discard table-exposed portions after unsafe holding.
servingSuggestions: Serve with rice and sharp or fresh banchan.

faq.question: Is black cod a true cod?
faq.answer: No. Black cod is a market name for sablefish; confirm the label.

faq.question: Why use a basket?
faq.answer: The rich delicate fillet can stick and break on open grates.

buyingCues: Fish is refrigerated on ice or frozen solid in intact packaging.
Odor is fresh and mild, never sour, rancid, fishy, or ammonia-like.
Flesh is firm without drying or discoloration at the edges.
seafoodPreparation.thawing: Thaw overnight in a covered refrigerator container. For rapid thawing, seal in a leakproof bag under cold water and cook immediately; never thaw on the counter.
seafoodPreparation.cleaningOrShellPreparation: Ask the seller to portion the fillet; inspect and remove detectable pin bones with clean tweezers, then sanitize the work area.
seafoodPreparation.drying: Pat all surfaces thoroughly dry with disposable paper towels and discard them immediately.
seafoodPreparation.grillSurfacePreparation: Preheat, clean, and lightly oil a fish basket or perforated grill pan.
seafoodPreparation.stickingPrevention: Keep skin on when available, dry thoroughly, oil lightly, and wait for the fish to release before turning.
seafoodPreparation.approximateTime: 10 to 12 minutes depending on thickness and grill output; thermometer verification controls.
donenessCues: Flesh is opaque and separates easily
Surface glaze is set but not burned
crossContactNotes: Use a dedicated raw-seafood board and utensils.
Reserve finishing glaze before raw-fish contact.
Use clean tools, thermometer, and platter for cooked fish.
